hld-resilience-ratelimiting.title: Resilience & Rate Limiting
hld-resilience-ratelimiting.intro: Designing for failure: timeouts, retries, breakers, bulkheads, and rate-limiting algorithms.
groups: Timeout Discipline

• EVERY network call gets a timeout; default-infinity causes cascade outages (thread pools exhaust waiting).
• Budget cascades: parent deadline split across hops with slack reserve; propagate deadlines in headers/contexts so children abort early.
• Timeout values from MEASUREMENT: p99.9 of dependency x small multiple; revisit after latency-profile changes.
• Ambiguous outcomes: timeout != failure — work may still complete! Resolution via idempotency keys + reconciliation queries — say this explicitly.
• Deadline propagation: gRPC deadlines, W3C traceparent, Go ctx cancellation — name your mechanism.
Retry Engineering

• Retry ONLY idempotent ops (or attach idempotency keys); retry only TRANSIENT classes (timeouts, 502/503/429-with-retry-after), never 4xx.
• Exponential backoff + full jitter: base x 2^n capped, random [0,cap] desynchronizing herds (AWS blog formula).
• Retry budgets: cap retries at N% globally — prevents retry storms converting brownouts into blackouts (Finagle pattern).
• Hedged requests: fire duplicate after p95 delay, take first winner — tail-latency killer for idempotent reads (Dean-Barroso paper).
• Interaction with LB: retries should hit DIFFERENT backend else you re-punish the same hot node.
Circuit Breakers & Bulkheads

• States: closed -> open after threshold -> half-open probe; per-dependency instances with dashboards.
• Fallbacks menu: cached value, default payload, feature-degradation flag, queued-deferred — graceful degradation BEFORE incidents.
• Bulkhead isolation: separate thread/connection pools per dependency — slow X can't starve healthy Y.
• Adaptive concurrency: measure inflight x RTT vs Little's-law ideal, shed excess.
• Load shedding hierarchy: reject lowest-priority first (batch < background < paying), return 503+Retry-After.
Rate Limiter Algorithms

• Fixed window: INCR+EXPIRE; boundary burst flaw (2x at edge).
• Sliding window log: exact timestamps, memory-heavy O(requests).
• Sliding window counter: weighted blend of current+previous (Cloudflare approach) — sweet-spot default.
• Token bucket: refill rate r, capacity b allowing bursts; versatile (cost-based limits: tokens = request weight).
• GCRA: single-timestamp elegance for telecom-grade precision.
Distributed Rate Limiting

• Central Redis Lua atomic check-and-decrement — simple, RTT + hotspot risk.
• Local shards + periodic sync: each node quota slice, sync drift — approximate but resilient.
• Consistent-hashing for affinity; fallback posture when limiter down (fail-open vs fail-closed by risk profile).
• Multi-dimension keys: user, API-key, IP, endpoint-class; nested limits composed.
• Cost-based quotas: LLM token counting / CPU-weighted endpoints — modern API necessity.
Chaos & Verification Culture

• Fault injection: kill instances, inject latency, exhaust pools — resilience claims VERIFIED (Netflix Chaos Kong heritage).
• Game days: rehearsed region-evacuation with shadowing; postmortem-driven scenario selection.
• Metrics: error-budget burn-rate alarms, breaker-open frequency, time-to-detect vs time-to-mitigate.
• Load-testing: production-shape replays (GoReplay) vs closed-loop distortion — methodology vocabulary.
• Drill: 'payment provider degrades to 8s' -> timeout-budget -> breaker -> queue-for-later -> user-messaging sequence.

hld-realtime-push.title: Real-Time & Push Systems
hld-realtime-push.intro: Live updates at scale: connection infrastructure, fan-out economics, presence, delivery guarantees.
groups: Connection Layer Architecture

• Gateway tier: persistent sockets (WS/SSE/WebTransport) + external state registry (conn-id -> gateway in Redis) enabling any-node routing.
• Scale: 100k-1M sockets/node depending language/frame-size; kernel tuning + io_uring/epoll; Go/Elixir stories.
• Shared pub/sub backbone makes gateways interchangeable (deploy-safe); stickiness only optimization.
• Reconnect storms: jittered exponential backoff CLIENT-side + server admission control (token-bucket).
• Auth: short-lived ticket over HTTPS -> upgrade validates -> per-message authorization for sensitive channels.
Fan-Out Economics

• Write-time fan-out: precompute timelines — fast reads, celebrity explosion (10M writes per tweet).
• Read-time merge: assemble on open — cheap writes, expensive reads; hybrid thresholds by follower-count (Twitter published).
• Push-notification tier: APNs/FCM own quotas; batching/digest policies reduce fatigue AND throttling.
• Room/channel: membership sets + message bus partitioned by channel-id; hot-channel read-cache (Discord pattern).
• Backpressure: bounded send queues, slow-consumer eviction — one slow phone can't OOM gateway.
Presence & State Sync

• Pipeline: heartbeats -> membership ZSET scored last-beat -> sweeper expires ghosts -> delta broadcasts to INTERESTED only.
• Multi-device aggregation rules (online if ANY device fresh).
• Collaborative apps: CRDT libraries (Yjs/Automerge); OT legacy comparison; cursors/presence ephemeral.
• Hydration: snapshot-on-connect + live-delta via sequence cursors; missed-events refill endpoint.
• Server-authoritative timestamps everywhere; client clocks only display.
Delivery Guarantees

• Classify: ephemeral (typing/presence — drop), durable-chat (at-least-once + dedupe + cursors), transactional-critical (payments NEVER via push alone).
• Ordering: per-conversation sequence numbers; gap triggers refill; cross-channel ordering abandoned deliberately.
• Offline queue: TTL per channel-type; unread-count rollups incremental; catch-up on reconnect.
• Read-markers: batched upstream sync; last-writer-wins per key.
• E2E encryption sketch (Signal-style double-ratchet) when privacy appears — scope honestly.
Notification Pipeline

• Stages: events -> orchestrator (dedupe, preferences, quiet-hours) -> adapters (push/email/SMS) -> providers with retry+DLQ -> receipt reconciliation.
• Idempotency keys prevent double-pushes; provider webhooks update delivered/opened states.
• Preference engine: opt-outs, frequency caps, snooze windows; compliance enforced centrally.
• Campaign bursts: 10M pushes -> provider rate limits -> sharded sender pool pacing.
• Observability: funnel conversion (queued->sent->delivered->opened), per-provider error taxonomies.

hld-hashing-probabilistic.title: Hashing & Probabilistic Structures
hld-hashing-probabilistic.intro: Consistent hashing, bloom filters, sketches — small structures answering big-scale questions.
groups: Consistent Hashing Complete

• mod-N resize moves ALL keys; ring hashing moves ~K/N only.
• Virtual nodes (100-200 per physical) smooth variance + enable heterogeneous weights.
• Rendezvous HRW: hash(key,node) for all, pick max — no ring metadata, O(N) lookup, great small clusters.
• Maglev lookup table: precomputed, minimal-disruption permutation — Google LB heritage.
• Bounded loads: ring + per-node max -> overflow clockwise (Vimeo/Cloudflare) preventing hotspots.
Bloom Filters & Variants

• FP rate approx (1-e^{-kn/m})^k; optimal k=0.7*bits-per-key; 10 bits/key ~1% FP.
• Apps: LSM gates, cache-admission, crawl-seen, malicious-URL checks.
• Counting bloom enables deletes; cuckoo filter: better space + deletion + cache-friendly.
• Scalable blooms grow with saturation; stable bloom for streams.
• Drill: 1B URLs @1% -> m~1.2GB, k~7 — do arithmetic live.
Sketch Zoo

• HyperLogLog: cardinality 0.81% SE @12KB (Redis PFADD).
• Count-Min Sketch: frequency estimates one-sided-overcounted; heavy-hitters via Space-Saving.
• Quantile: t-digest/DDSketch computing p99s across merged distributed agents.
• Map: membership -> bloom, frequency -> CMS, cardinality -> HLL, rank -> t-digest.
• Error direction: CMS overestimates-only (safe for admission); choose by tolerance.
Sharding Math & Hot Keys

• Salt hotkeys (key{n%16} sub-shards), aggregate on read; tradeoffs kill range-scans.
• Celebrity: replicate read-hot across followers + local caches; write-hot split into accumulators.
• Jump/truncated hashes: stateless shard-count changes.
• Rebalancing estimate: ring w/vnodes ~K/N moved.
• Geo-aware: ring per-region + prefix steering; data residency layered atop.
Probabilistic Interview Framing

• Frame as accuracy-vs-resources: exact top-100 in MBs vs estimate all in KBs at +/-2%.
• Pipeline: bloom-gate -> CMS-count -> HLL-unique -> t-digest-latencies.
• Failure modes: bloom FP harmless for admission, CMS saturation grow depth, HLL sparse encoding.
• Anchors: Redis PFCOUNT, Prometheus quantile caveats, Cloudflare CM sketches.
• Drills: unique-IP (HLL), trending-tags (CMS+SpaceSaving), URL filter (bloom math), mergeable p99 (DDSketch).

hld-observability-security.title: Observability & Security
hld-observability-security.intro: Metrics/logs/traces done right, SLO engineering, authN/Z architecture, secrets, audit trails.
groups: Three Pillars Done Right

• Metrics: counters/histograms (Prometheus), label-cardinality discipline, recording rules.
• Logs: structured JSON with trace/correlation ids; sampling; retention tiering; NEVER log secrets/PII.
• Traces: W3C traceparent propagation; head-vs-tail sampling (tail captures errors/slow — useful).
• Exemplars: histogram bucket <-> trace bridges anomaly -> root-cause (Grafana Tempo).
• Horror story: user-id-as-label killed clusters — aggregate-first principle.
SLO Engineering & Alerting

• SLIs user-centric: availability, latency p99 at CLIENT edge, freshness.
• Error budgets: burn-rate alerts (14.4x/1h fast + 6x/6h slow — Google Workbook recipe).
• Page ONLY user-impacting burn; tickets for trends; dashboards for exploration.
• Capacity alerts: disk-full-in-14d forecasts, not static 80%.
• Blameless postmortems with action-items tracked to closure.
AuthN/AuthZ Architecture

• Triangle: human SSO (OIDC), service mTLS/JWT, workload identity (SPIFFE).
• Short-lived access + refresh rotation; audience-bound; JWKS rotation; revocation via TTL.
• RBAC -> ABAC (OPA/Cedar) -> ReBAC (Zanzibar/SpiceDB) by complexity.
• Policy-as-code repos with tests; decision logs audited.
• Edge enforcement: gateway basic scopes, services re-verify audience (zero-trust).
Secrets & Key Management

• Lifecycle: generation, storage (Vault/KMS/HSM), automated rotation, tested revocation.
• Envelope encryption: DEKs + KEKs; KMS calls amortized via local cache.
• Internal PKI: Vault/step-ca, short-lived certs auto-renewed.
• Leakage runbook: secret-scan CI, rotate-assume-breached, git-history purge reality.
• Sealed-secrets/SOPS for k8s GitOps flows.
Audit, Compliance & Abuse

• Append-only security events with actor/target/context; immutable storage for regulated retention.
• Anomaly hooks: impossible-travel, privilege-escalation, unusual exports — SIEM ingestion.
• Abuse: credential-stuffing walls (rate+fingerprint); bot management at edge.
• Privacy: field-level encryption, purpose-bound access logging, crypto-shredding for GDPR.
• SOC2 evidence automation; subprocessor list; data-residency pinning.

hld-back-of-envelope.title: Back-of-Envelope Estimation
hld-back-of-envelope.intro: Rapid capacity math: translate requirements into QPS, storage, bandwidth, and memory numbers before drawing diagrams.
groups: Estimation Framework

• Flow: requirements -> users -> QPS (avg+peak) -> bytes/request -> bandwidth -> storage -> memory -> cost.
• Peak vs avg: 3x peak is standard; 10x for batch/integration, 50x for flash-sale scenarios — state assumptions explicitly.
• Read:write ratio: social 100:1, chat 5:1, IoT ingest 10:1, CRUD app 10:1 — drives cache vs queue decisions.
• Growth model: linear vs viral vs seasonal; multiply final numbers by 2-3x headroom.
• Arithmetic fluency: 1M DAU x 10 req/day = ~120 QPS avg; 1B rows x 500B = 500GB raw; SSD ~$0.10/GB-month.
Traffic & Bandwidth

• Users -> QPS: MAU/30/86400 = avg concurrent; multiply by requests-per-session.
• Payload sizes: JSON API ~1-5KB, image ~200KB, video chunk ~2-5MB, CDN static ~50KB.
• Bandwidth = QPS x avg_response_size x (1 + read_replication_factor).
• Egress pricing: AWS ~$0.09/GB; multi-CDN egress reduction is a cost lever.
• WebSocket: concurrent_conns x heartbeat_interval -> sustained Kbps; burst amplification factor 2-5x.
Storage Estimation

• Row math: num_objects x avg_row_size x years x replication_factor x overhead (1.3-2x).
• Index overhead: 1.5-3x raw data depending number of secondary indexes + B-tree fill factor.
• Partition boundaries: keep partitions under 100GB for hot data; cold data can be larger in data lake.
• Time-series: 1 metric x 10s interval = ~3M points/year x 8B = ~24MB/year per metric.
• Blob: video = views x resolution x duration; 10M daily views x 10s 720p ~30-50TB/day.
Memory & Cache Sizing

• Hot set: active_users x avg_metadata_size; pin in Redis with TTL.
• Cache hit-rate math: 95% hit means 5% miss hitting origin; origin capacity = total_QPS x 0.05.
• Connection pools: postprocess = num_app_nodes x pool_size_per_node; must fit DB max_connections.
• Bloom filter sizing: 10 bits/key for 1% FP; 1B keys -> 1.25GB.
• Working set: if fits in RAM -> SSD offload unnecessary; if 10x RAM -> tiered storage mandatory.
Interview Execution

• Time-box: 2-3 min estimation at START of interview; write numbers on board; refer back throughout.
• Anchor with real-world: 'Instagram serves 2B photos/day' or 'Twitter processes 500M tweets/day' — calibrates.
• Explicit assumptions list: write them down so interviewer can correct early ('assume 300M MAU, is that right?').
• Scale-up narrative: 'at 10K QPS single Postgres handles it; at 100K QPS add read replicas; at 1M QPS shard by user_id' — show progression.
• Cost awareness: rough $/month estimates for storage+compute+egress; mention reserved instances vs on-demand tradeoffs.

hld-playbook-case-studies.title: Playbook & Case Studies
hld-playbook-case-studies.intro: Real-world architecture case studies: what companies built, why, and lessons learned — the senior engineering interview edge.
groups: Social Feed Systems

• Twitter timeline: fan-out-on-write (pull model) for <10K followers, pull-on-read (merge) for celebrities — hybrid threshold published 2013.
• Facebook News Feed: ranked by EdgeRank (affinity x weight x time_decay); ML re-ranking at read-time; real-time updates via LiveData.
• Instagram: pulled MySQL with memcache + delayed fanout for large followers; later moved to Kafka-based fanout.
• Common lessons: write amplification of fan-out-on-write (celebrity problem), consistency tradeoffs acceptable for feeds (eventual is fine), storage explosion of precomputed timelines.
Messaging & Chat Systems

• WhatsApp: Erlang-based, 2M connections/machine, mnesia for small state, MySQL for messages, push via APNs/FCM.
• Discord: Go + Rust services, Elixir for voice (soft real-time), Cassandra for message storage, Redis for presence.
• Slack: single-channel-adjacent model, Molt/Manta for message storage, eventual consistency accepted, WebSocket + long-polling fallback.
• Lessons: message ordering is per-conversation (not global), offline storage + sync protocol critical, read receipts are expensive (fan-out on read).
Search & Recommendation

• Google search: inverted index sharded by document, MapReduce-era batch, real-time signals via streaming.
• Netflix: row-based personalization (taste vectors), contextual bandits for thumbnails, A/B testing infrastructure as core platform.
• Spotify: Explore/Exploit via multi-armed bandits, collaborative filtering + content-based hybrid, podcast ranking separate pipeline.
• Common: two-tower retrieval + scoring pipeline, A/B testing as first-class capability, offline metrics (NDCG/MAP) vs online (CTR/engagement).
Infrastructure Case Studies

• AWS S3: availability-first design, 11 nines durability via replication, eventual consistency (now read-after-write), bucket policies as access control.
• Netflix: Chaos Monkey, circuit breakers, zone-aware routing, bulk migration to cloud (2008-2016), ZUUL edge.
• Uber: microservices explosion (10K+), domain-oriented microservice architecture (DOMA) as consolidation, cab-signaling real-time via custom protocols.
• Lessons: complexity cost of microservices (Netflix calmed down), chaos testing culture as competitive advantage, platform teams as force multiplier.
Interview Integration

• Case study as evidence: 'Twitter's hybrid fanout tells us...' — connects theory to practice.
• Failure mode recall: 'Remember Uber's 2017 outage was cascading via service mesh — that's why we need bulkhead isolation.'
• Numbers as credibility: cite real metrics (WhatsApp 2M conn/machine, S3 11 nines) — demonstrates engineering depth.
• Tradeoff storytelling: 'Netflix chose eventual consistency for recommendations because immediate consistency isn't worth 10x latency' — shows judgment.
• Anti-pattern: name-dropping without understanding; better to deeply know 3 case studies than surface 10.
